item.title: Willo Alarms and Locking Mechanisms
item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-09-16

In accordance with Procurement Policy Board Rule Section 3-05, the New York City Department of Correction (DOC) intends to enter into a sole source agreement with Willo Products Company, LLC. The purpose of this agreement is to procure alarms and locking mechanisms vital to the ongoing maintenance and upgrade of the DOCs detention locking systems.
 

The DOC is currently replacing and upgrading cell doors throughout its facilities to comply with modern correctional standards. This procurement will encompass high security locking systems, including the Wedge, Tamper Alarm, Gripper, and High-intensity LED light Lock Receivers.

item.title: Board of Correction Public Meeting
item.description:
Board of Correction | Public Hearings and Meetings | Meeting | Hearing: 2026-09-09

The New York City Board of Correction will hold a public meeting on Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 1:00pm. The meeting with be held in the auditorium located on the 2nd floor of 125 Worth Street. The Board will discuss issues impacting the New York City jail system.

More information is available on the Board's website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/boc/meetings/2026-meetings.page

                                                  

  • Wheelchair Access. The venue has an accessible entrance on Lafayette Street and elevators. There are accessible bathrooms on the first floor of the building.
  • Assistive Listening Systems (ALS). ALS is not currently in place at the 125 Worth Street Second Floor Auditorium.

item.title: Financial Deposits and Kiosk Services
item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Award | $1 | Vendor: Keefe Commissary Network LLC

The New York City Department of Correction (DOC) is seeking a vendor to provide financial deposit services for the benefit of people in custody (PICs). DOC would like to facilitate the deposit of these funds (excluding bail payments) into PIC commissary accounts through various methods such as internet, mobile phone, third-party kiosks, and cash at DOC cashier locations, walk-in third party locations (i.e. Western Union, Money Gram, etc.).

item.title: Vertical Hydroponic Farm
item.description:
Correction | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-08-14

In accordance with Procurement Policy Board Rule Section 3-05, the New York City Department of Correction (DOC) intends to enter into a sole source agreement with FarmBox Foods LLC. The purpose of this agreement is to procure a Vertical Hydroponic Farm for Persons-in-Custody (PICs) to develop a skill that can be utilized when being released from custody.

The Department of Correction seeks to revitalize its Workforce Development Unit to include new and innovative trades and skill building classes that directly relate to re-entry and reduced recidivism.  Based on an evaluation of potential trades and skills that are felony friendly, DOC believes that there is a gap in services as it pertains to urban agriculture, community gardening, local and small business entrepreneurship, local and small business prospectives, and culinary arts.  The investment in FarmBox Foods would allow the Department to build and develop two tracks of Workforce Development.  One is for participants who would tend to the literal garden and hydroponic farm, and the other is associated with our culinary arts program and …

In accordance with Procurement Policy Board Rule Section 3-05, the New York City Department of Correction (DOC) intends to enter into a sole source agreement with Willo Products Company, LLC. The purpose of this agreement is to procure psychological test supplies.

These assessments are specialized objective tests designed to evaluate various dimensions of psychological suitability among officer candidates, including mental health, psychological history, and
personality traits. They are widely recognized as the gold standard in the evaluation of police and public safety personnel.

Given that the report is created from PsyQ data that is collected by means of a copyrighted answer sheet and/or scoring software that was designed by Johnson, Roberts, and Associates, Inc. All PsyQ supplies and software are copyrighted, proprietary products that are available only from Johnson, Roberts, and Associates, Inc. Other vendors do not offer the proprietary selection reports required for psychological evaluations of this specialized population.
